Police said an operation took place near the town of Bautzen. "A police operation is taking place," a police spokesperson told German tabloid Bild . "For tactical reasons, we cannot comment on it." Local public broadcaster MDR meanwhile reported that one of the searches took place near the village of Schleife, close to the state border with Brandenburg . Saxony's state interior minister, Armin Schuster, told the DPA news agency that "unknown explosive contraptions" had been discovered. "Police secured four objects at two locations and are proceeding with their defusal," he said. The police operations in Saxony took place almost simultaneously with the storming of a vehicle linked to sabotage attempts in the western state of North Rhine-Westphalia . "Saxon security services are coordinating closely with those in other affected states," said Schuster. https://p.dw.com/p/5Le0W Skip next section German police storm sabotage suspect's vehicle 09/04/2026 September 4, 2026 German police storm sabotage suspect's vehicle Armed officers from Germany 's elite Spezialeinsatzkommando (SEK) police unit located and stormed a truck thought to belong a man suspected of carrying out acts of sabotage against electrical infrastructure this week (see below). The truck was located in the village of Niederzier near the town of Düren, in between the cities of Aachen and Cologne in the western state of North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW). One of the substations that was attacked was in the nearby town of Bergheim. The vehicle was found to be empty and appeared to have been converted into a motorhome. The suspect is believed to have fled on foot. NRW state Interior Minister Herbert Reul confirmed the operation and said the man would "not get far." Niederzier is close to a large and controversial surface mine on the site of the ancient Hambach Forest (Hambacher Forst) , most of which has been cleared to make way for mining operations. The location has been the site of several occupations by environmental activists over the past 15 years, leading to clashes with police and arrests. In a letter claiming responsibility for this week's sabotage efforts, the suspect sought by police said he was motivated by environmental concerns, in particular the "fight against fossil fuels." German federal interior minister Alexander Dobrindt also said earlier (see below) that authorities suspected "climate extremism." The increase was mainly driven by an "exceptionally high volume" of large-scale orders for ships, railway rolling stock and aircraft, according to a Destatis press release . Industrial orders serve as an indicator of future business activity, and the recent increase is being interpreted by some analysts as a sign Germany's struggling economy is starting to recover . This week, the Ifo and RWI economic research institutes both sharply revised their 2026 GDP growth forecasts higher by 1.3 to 1.4% "It has been a long while since such we have had such positive headlines about the German economy," LBBW bank analyst Jens-Oliver Niklasch told AFP news agency. Factors including high energy prices, the rise of Chinese exports in competitive markets, and a faltering automotive sector have all weighed heavily on Germany's growth in recent years. Chancellor Friedrich Merz has vowed to borrow and spend hundreds of billions of euros in the coming years to boost industrial growth, mainly through defense and infrastructure.
